name: Michael Rees
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Rees is cofounder and co-president of Blue Owl, which manages $250 billion and formed in 2021 when his Dyal Capital merged with Owl Rock Capital.
Dyal, since renamed Blue Owl GP Strategic Capital, is known for buying minority stakes in more than 60 other private equity firms.
Rees' division also invests in professional sports, with a fund that owns pieces of the NBA's Phoenix Suns, Sacramento Kings and Atlanta Hawks.
Rees still heads Blue Owl GP Strategic Capital, which oversees $66 billion. The rest of the firm's assets are in private credit and real estate.
Rees spent seven years at Lehman Brothers and started Dyal as a subsidiary of Neuberger Berman, which bought out parts of the bankrupt Lehman in 2009.

name: Judith Neilson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2017-2021); Hurun Global (2018-2020)
forbes_bio: Neilson is the ex-wife of billionaire Kerr Neilson and is also a billionaire. She's reported to have her own property portfolio.
She holds a stake in international equities manager Platinum Asset Management, founded in 1994 by her former husband.
The Zimbabwe-born former graphic designer is founder and director of Sydney's White Rabbit Gallery.
The gallery showcases one of the world's biggest collections of contemporary Chinese art post-2000.
She kickstarted another Sydney art gallery and a performance space called Phoenix.

name: Caspar Callerström
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Caspar Callerström joined Swedish investment company EQT AB in 1996.
Callerström is chief operating officer and partner at now publicly traded EQT, which has roughly $81 billion in assets under management.
EQT primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
EQT has minted seven billionaires, nearly as many as Google or Facebook.
Privately, Callerstrom is one of the founding members of a group of financial elites that backs the Swedish football club Djurgårdens IF.

name: Chang Chung-Hsing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun China (2024-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Chang Chung-Hsing is the chairman of Taichung-based Apex Dynamics.
He founded the company in 1987 as a maker of robotic arms, and has built it into one of the world's largest suppliers of high-precision gearboxes.
Apex listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 2022.
It also owns Millennium Vee Hotel Taichung, operated in partnership with Singapore's Millennium Hotels & Resorts, one of the oldest international-brand hotels in central Taiwan.

name: Hartono Kweefanus
forbes_bio: Indonesian-born Hartono Kweefanus is chairman of Monde Nissin, a food manufacturer based in the Philippines known for its instant noodles and snacks.
Kweefanus' wealth lies in a significant personal stake in the company.
His late father cofounded Monde Nissin in 1979 together with Betty Ang, the company's president.
Kweefanus is the brother-in-law of Ang, who's also among the richest people in the Philippines.
Monde Nissin raised $1.1 billion in June 2021, in what was the country's biggest IPO.

name: Tran Ba Duong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2018-2024); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Tran Ba Duong got his start working at an auto repair factory in the 1980s and eventually worked his way up to management.
He founded Truong Hai Group, also known as Thaco, in 1997; it initially sold cars and later started assembling cars for foreign brands such as Kia, Mazda and Peugeot.
His company's turning point came in 2008, when Jardine Cycle and Carriage, a car distributor in Singapore, bought a stake in it.
Thaco is now one of the biggest conglomerates in Vietnam with interests in automobiles, real estates, agriculture and logistics.
forbes_facts: He received the EY Asean Entrepreneurial Excellence Award in 2020.
Tran is known to control every little detail of his business and often requests meetings with the management in the evenings and on weekends.

name: Simon Xie
forbes_bio: Simon Xie is a cofounder of China e-commerce giant Alibaba Group.
Prior to joining Alibaba Group, he got an engineering degree from Shenyang University of Technology and did financial work at a state-run company.

name: Marc Zahr
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Marc Zahr is a co-president of Blue Owl, an investment firm with $250 billion in assets under management, and oversees its real assets business.
Zahr founded real estate investment firm Oak Street in 2009, and Blue Owl bought the firm in December 2021 for $950 million.
Oak Street managed $12.4 billion in assets at the time of the acquisition, and under Blue Owl the segment has grown to $49 billion.
Zahr's business is the market leader in triple net leases, a type of commercial lease requiring tenants to pay expenses like taxes and maintenance.
